solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Inattentive and confused best man denied dropping ecstasy

indicators.note: the letters are muddled up
DENIED lets go of one of its letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
DENIED without one E, the letter for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A groom's best man, careless and muddled, is refused something now that he has given up the drug.
explanation.walkthrough: E for ecstasy is a standard crossword abbreviation. Once one E leaves DENIED, the remaining letters join BEST MAN to make the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone absent-minded is not paying attention, which is what inattentive means.

clue.text: Downbeat, is hoodlum stifling sneeze?

indicators.note: the outer words smother the answer, holding it inside them

blocks.note: the letters run from the tail of 'Downbeat', through 'is', into the head of 'hoodlum'

explanation.surface: A glum thug is trying to hold in a sneeze.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma hides the join: the answer starts in the last letters of 'Downbeat' and runs across 'is' into 'hoodlum'.
explanation.definitionFit: ATISHOO is the British spelling of the sound of a sneeze, like the American 'achoo'.

clue.text: Sister extremely likely to accept award without histrionics

indicators.note: only the extremes, the first and last letters, of 'likely' are used
to accept an award is to take it in, so SR takes OBE inside it

blocks.note: Sr is the abbreviation for Sister, as in a nun's title
the OBE, a British honour (Officer of the Order of the British Empire)
first and last letters of LIKELY

explanation.surface: A sister is likely to receive an honour without making a fuss about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is an honour given by the British monarch, so 'award' is a fair way to clue it.
explanation.definitionFit: To act soberly is to act calmly and seriously, without histrionics.

clue.text: With European ex-con, I’m travelling around part of the US

indicators.note: the letters move about and end up in a new order

blocks.note: w is the abbreviation for with
E = European
anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A released prisoner tells how he is touring America with a European companion.
explanation.walkthrough: Every letter of the fodder is used, including the W from 'With' and the E from 'European'; the apostrophe in I'm is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: New Mexico is a state in the south-west of the US.

clue.text: Soldiers and miners climbing peak

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters go upward, so they read backwards

blocks.note: OR = other ranks, ordinary soldiers
the NUM, the British National Union of Mineworkers

explanation.surface: A group of soldiers and miners go up a mountain together.
explanation.walkthrough: A Munro is a Scottish mountain over 3,000 feet high; the NUM is the British miners' union.
explanation.definitionFit: A Munro is a peak, one of the Scottish mountains over 3,000 feet that hillwalkers collect.

clue.text: Swapping the headings of domesticated horse’s ID

indicators.note: the first letters of the two words change places

blocks.note: tame = domesticated; its T is swapped for the N heading the next word
a nag is a horse; its N is swapped for the T heading TAME

explanation.surface: Someone is fiddling with the labels on a pet horse's identity tag.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in horse's is the 'is' of 'horse is ID', so the swap of the two words' first letters gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A name tag shows who you are, so it is a form of ID.

clue.text: Content to be at rear of vessel from China?

indicators.note: the contents of 'be at', its inside letters

blocks.note: the inside of B(EA)T
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone is happy to sit at the back of a boat sailing from China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like happy; it is the insides of 'be at'. The question mark flags that China is only one example of somewhere eastern.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: China lies in the Far East, so anything from there is one instance of eastern, as the question mark admits.

clue.text: Is painful red bum revealing mistake?

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means bad or faulty, so the letters are broken up

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a sore red behind gives something away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' reads as the backside, a picture of a painful red rear; it is really the adjective meaning bad, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Freudian slip is a mistake in speech thought to reveal a hidden wish.

clue.text: Sky feature artist visiting the East End?

indicators.note: the artist is in a place, so IN is placed next to BOW

blocks.note: RA = Royal Academician
someone visiting a place is in it
Bow is a district in London's East End

explanation.surface: A painter heads to the East End of London, looking for something in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditionally working-class part of east London, and Bow is one of its districts.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainbow is an arc of colours seen in the sky.

clue.text: Saint I spotted coming back, welcoming maiden goddess

indicators.note: the letters return, reading from right to left
the reversed letters take M in

blocks.note: S = saint
taken as written
spotted = seen
M = maiden, an over with no runs in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A saint says she saw a goddess return and greet a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: S I SEEN reversed is NEESIS, and M goes in after NE. 'Maiden' looks like a young woman, but it gives M, the cricket abbreviation for an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A proper name: in Greek myth Nemesis was the goddess who punished arrogance, and her name later came to mean any unbeatable rival.

clue.text: Small indication Tesla lease saves nothing for city

indicators.note: TOKEN holds on to the O, keeping it inside

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels
a token is a sign or indication
O = zero, nothing
T is the symbol for the tesla, a unit of magnetic flux density
to lease is to rent

explanation.surface: A small sign that a Tesla car lease costs nothing turns up for someone in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tesla' looks like the car maker, but it gives T, the symbol for the unit of magnetic flux density. O goes inside TOKEN, between the E and the N. Stoke-on-Trent is a city in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoke-on-Trent is a city in Staffordshire, England, famous for pottery.

clue.text: Throw our hens nuts

indicators.note: nuts = crazy, so the letters go wild

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to throw nuts to our chickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw' looks like an order to toss something to the hens; it is the definition, as a horse throws its rider.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the riding sense: a horse that throws its rider has knocked them out of the saddle.

clue.text: Busy part of year initially destroyed self-confidence

indicators.note: the first letter of MONTH is removed

blocks.note: a month is part of a year; lose its M
ego = sense of self-worth

explanation.surface: A hectic stretch of the year ruined someone's confidence from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks like 'at first', but it tells you the first letter of MONTH is the one destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a person constantly moving from one task to the next is busy.

clue.text: Cream horn barely fills climber

indicators.note: HORN is stripped bare, losing its outer letters
the remaining OR goes inside IVY

blocks.note: ivy is a climbing plant
HORN without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cream horn pastry is stuffed into a climber's pack.
explanation.walkthrough: A cream horn is a British pastry, and 'Cream' looks like its filling; it is the colour. 'Barely' means stripped bare, not scarcely.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivory is a creamy off-white colour.

clue.text: I clipped information about energy poverty

indicators.note: INDIA has its end cut off
about gives C, for circa, placed next in line

blocks.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet; clip off the A
gen is British slang for information
c = circa, about
E = energy, as in physics

explanation.surface: Someone cut short a report on fuel poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: The key is that 'I' stands for INDIA in the phonetic alphabet, so clipping it gives INDI. Gen is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from Latin indigere, to be in need: the formal word for lacking the necessities of life.

clue.text: Change of course leaves learner failing

indicators.note: L departs from DEFLECTION

blocks.note: DEFLECTION, a change of course, minus L
L = learner, from the L-plates on a British learner driver's car; this is the letter removed

explanation.surface: A student drops out of a course and fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of course' reads like switching university courses; it means a deflection, a change of direction. Defection in the older sense means a failing or shortcoming.
explanation.definitionFit: Defection can mean a failure in duty, a falling away, so it fits 'failing' as a noun.

clue.text: Farce is one of Shakespeare’s First Folio plays

indicators.note: take the first letter of Shakespeare's
the letters play about, rearranging

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
the first letter of Shakespeare
F = folio

explanation.surface: A claim that a farce is one of the plays in Shakespeare's First Folio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shakespeare's First Folio' is the 1623 collected edition of his plays, and it reads as one name; it splits into S, a first letter, and F for folio. Noises Off is a farce by Michael Frayn.
explanation.definitionFit: Noises Off is a famous stage farce by Michael Frayn.

clue.text: Opening of concerto penned by revolutionary composer missing middle tooth

indicators.note: take the first letter of concerto
C is written inside the composer
the composer turns round, reading backwards
the centre letter of the seven is dropped

blocks.note: first letter of CONCERTO
ROSSINI reversed is INISSOR; drop its middle S

explanation.surface: The opening of a concerto was written by a radical composer who has lost a front tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: Rossini, the Italian opera composer, is the one to find. 'Revolutionary' looks like a radical, but it means turned right round.
explanation.definitionFit: An incisor is one of the cutting teeth at the front of the mouth.

clue.text: Releasing former partner on drugs with daughter, not son

indicators.note: 'with' means accompanied by, so the daughter's D comes into the word
'not son' refuses the son, so his S is the letter that goes

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner

blocks.clueFragment: on drugs with daughter, not son
blocks.note: USING (on drugs) with D for daughter in place of S for son

explanation.surface: A former partner, high on drugs, is released along with their daughter but not their son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Releasing' looks like letting someone go; it is the definition, as in giving off a liquid or smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Exuding means giving off or releasing, as a plant exudes sap.

clue.text: Bird is near lions on a regular basis

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals, every second one

blocks.note: i(S) n(E) a(R) l(I) o(N)s

explanation.surface: A bird sits close to lions every now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters of 'is near lions'.
explanation.definitionFit: The serin is a small yellow finch of Europe.

clue.text: Old vehicle carrying army corps and Zulu is flipping freezing

indicators.note: RE and Z ride along with the bus
the whole string flips over, reading backwards

blocks.note: O = old
RE = Royal Engineers, a British army corps
Zulu is Z in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An old truck carrying troops and a Zulu warrior flips over in the icy cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole string is built first and then turned round as one. 'Flipping' also reads as a mild British swear word, as in 'flipping freezing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Subzero means below zero degrees, which is freezing.

clue.text: Act carefree to turn on one retired barrister

indicators.note: the barrister withdraws, going backwards

blocks.note: to roll is to turn over
I = one, the Roman numeral
a KC is a King's Counsel, a senior British barrister

explanation.surface: Someone is told to relax and turn on a lawyer who has left the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A KC (King's Counsel) is a senior barrister in Britain. 'Retired' looks like stopped working, but it turns KC into CK.
explanation.definitionFit: To rollick is to play or behave in a carefree, boisterous way.

clue.text: Caught someone without coat

indicators.note: caught as in heard, 'I didn't catch what you said'

blocks.note: a lacker is someone who lacks, who goes without

explanation.surface: Someone is caught out in the cold with no coat on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like arrested, but it means heard. 'Coat' looks like the garment; it is a layer of paint or varnish.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacquer is a glossy varnish applied as a coat.

clue.text: Severely criticise emperor taking over from the south

indicators.note: an emperor taking something holds it, so TSAR holds O inside
in a down clue, reading from the bottom up means backwards

blocks.note: a tsar was the Russian emperor
O = over, in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: Critics lay into an emperor who seizes power, moving up from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: TSA(O)R read upward from the bottom gives ROAST. 'Over' looks like part of 'taking over'; it is the cricket O.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal sense: putting someone over the fire, figuratively, as in a comedy roast or a boss roasting an employee.

clue.text: Moving gear’s left to the right person at last

indicators.note: moving something shifts its position, so one letter of the gear is relocated
the L, for left, goes further right

blocks.note: clobber is British slang for clothes or gear; move its L two places right

explanation.surface: Someone moving kit shifts it from left to right.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is the foot-shaped block a shoemaker works on, so 'person at last' is a cobbler, not someone who has finally arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler mends shoes working at a last, so is literally a person at a last.

clue.text: Private investigators spy agency guarding final bit of Amazon basin

indicators.note: a guard surrounds what it protects, so CIA closes round N
take the last letter of Amazon

blocks.note: PI = private investigator, plural PIs
the CIA, the US Central Intelligence Agency
last letter of AMAZON

explanation.surface: Detectives and spies watch over the lower reaches of the Amazon basin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazon basin' looks like one geographical phrase, but 'basin' is the definition. A piscina is a stone basin near a church altar.
explanation.definitionFit: A piscina is a stone basin in a church, used for washing the communion vessels.

clue.text: From a peninsula, live broadcast about popular bars

indicators.note: about as in 'about turn', a turn to face the other way, so AIR reads backwards
IN shuts the other letters in, like prison bars

blocks.note: in = fashionable, popular
to live is to be
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A live broadcast is coming from popular bars on a peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' looks like pubs; it is a verb, shutting the other letters in the way bars close a cell. The Iberian peninsula holds Spain and Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberian means from the Iberian peninsula, Spain and Portugal.

clue.text: Socially aware, boring badger in novel

indicators.note: RIGHT-ON drills its way into BROCK

blocks.note: brock is an old name for the badger
right-on = socially and politically aware

explanation.surface: A socially conscious novel features a dull badger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like dull; it means drilling into. B(RIGHT ON)ROCK. Brighton Rock is Graham Greene's 1938 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A title as the definition: Graham Greene's 1938 thriller about the gangster Pinkie, named after the stick of seaside candy.
